title: Pointwise Minimax Rates for CATE in a Latent Covariate Observed with Error
banked_reason: D0.5 decision and math referees passed, but the cold general referee graded the delivered paper subfield below the required field floor (paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4; salvageable=false).
gap_reasons: The result is nevertheless confined to an engineered benchmark with uniform circular design, a known exact error multiplier, binary outcomes, and fixed smoothness, which limits its reach beyond this experiment.

The advertised finite-sample interval is not operationally reproducible as written because C_up is specified only through an instruction to combine norm envelopes rather than an explicit formula or numerical value, while the resulting n_0 is potentially enormous.

The STAR*D relevance remains purely motivational, with no computation showing useful constants or attainable interval widths in a realistic regime; these scope and evidence limitations constrain the projected paper score.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived the observable inverse-pair upper bound and a rotating-frame mixture lower bound, yielding matching n^(-1/24) point-risk and honest connected-interval-length rates in the fixed latent-score experiment. Both D0.5 correctness panels passed with no findings. The general referee graded the delivered scope subfield, below the required field floor; broader design or channel results would require a new research anchor.
tldr: The value \(\tau_P(1/2)\) of the unique periodic Lipschitz latent CATE representative has exact pointwise minimax absolute-risk and finite-sample honest connected-interval-length order \(n^{-1/24}\). The explicit observed-score inverse-pair estimator and Chebyshev interval attain the upper rate. For the converse, a weighted two-cell periodic frame is constructed analytically: its single elements and adjacent products annihilate both lifted wrapped-Laplace moments, so their convolutions remain cell-local and their four-adjacent-cell squared Gram is \(O(h\delta^9)\). A legal four-mark Bernoulli product mixture at \(h\asymp n^{-1/24}\) and \(\delta\asymp h^5\) then has bounded chi-square distance and target separation of order \(h\). The exact exponent \(1/24\) is strictly larger than the separate-arm EIV exponent \(1/52\); the gain comes from cancellation of the first-order propensity and baseline increments in the pair contrast.
gap: Observed-covariate CATE minimax theory does not survive an inverse observation channel unchanged, while classical EIV regression theory estimates one arm at a time and misses causal nuisance cancellation. Existing EIV bands are asymptotic and single-regression, and the public 2026 mismeasured-CATE paper does not claim a fixed-class minimax or honest-length frontier.
fill: The project defines the inverse operator on the marked-density range, constructs arbitrary-bandwidth torus kernels, proves their exact scaling and twice-inverted norm bounds, and derives the observable inverse-pair MSE bound and finite-sample honest interval for the value at (x_0) of the unique periodic Lipschitz representative. It then resolves the weighted rotating-frame certificate to determine the exact common pointwise-risk and honest-length exponent on the same fixed class.
